findings.source_passage: Deep into distant woodlands winds a mazy way, reaching to overlapping spurs of mountains bathed in their hill-side blue.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is the rhetorical centrepiece of the landscape-painting passage—its sinuous syntax enacts the 'mazy way' it describes. Without it, the Saco paragraph jumps abruptly from cattle and cottage smoke to 'But though the picture lies thus tranced,' losing the hypnotic build-up that earns the payoff about the shepherd's eye on the stream.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Deep into distant woodlands winds a mazy way, reaching to overlapping spurs of mountains bathed in their hill-side blue.' between the cottage-smoke sentence and 'But though the picture lies thus tranced.'

findings.source_passage: Why did the poor poet of Tennessee, upon suddenly receiving two handfuls of silver, deliberate whether to buy him a coat, which he sadly needed, or invest his money in a pedestrian trip to Rockaway Beach?
findings.why_it_matters: This comic, satirical question is a signature specimen of Ishmael's ironic voice—mixing high rhetoric with a deliberately bathetic, specific anecdote. Its omission flattens the rhetorical catalogue from five questions to four and removes the only humorous beat in the series, thinning the voice-defining register.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the Tennessee-poet question in its original position between the Niagara question and the 'robust healthy boy' question.

findings.source_passage: cooled by breezes, which a few hours previous were out of sight of land.
findings.why_it_matters: The clause extends the Battery description outward to the open sea and enacts the very pull toward the horizon Ishmael is anatomising; its loss slightly deflates the passage's thematic resonance.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'and cooled by breezes, which a few hours previous were out of sight of land' after 'washed by waves' in the Manhattoes paragraph.

findings.source_passage: It is out of the idolatrous dotings of the old Egyptians upon broiled ibis and roasted river horse, that you see the mummies of those creatures in their huge bake-houses the pyramids.
findings.source_locator: Passenger/cook/sailor digression, end of the broiled-fowl riff
findings.why_it_matters: This mock-erudite non-sequitur is classic Ishmael—absurdist digression used to deflate self-importance—and its loss shortens an already-trimmed paragraph, removing a characteristic comic cadence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Egyptian/pyramids sentence as the closing beat of the broiled-fowl passage.

findings.source_passage: cajoling me into the delusion that it was a choice resulting from my own unbiased freewill and discriminating judgment.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses to 'cajoling me into the delusion that it was my own choice,' losing the ironic legalism of 'unbiased freewill and discriminating judgment' which is part of Ishmael's mock-philosophical voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full phrase: 'cajoling me into the delusion that it was a choice resulting from my own unbiased freewill and discriminating judgment.'

summary: The draft preserves all high-priority signatures (opening paragraph, Narcissus, Providence bill, flood-gates closing) verbatim or near-verbatim; the five findings are two medium-level voice flattenings (omitted Saco woodland sentence and Tennessee-poet question) and three low-level cuts, none rising to regeneration threshold individually, and the medium count does not reach three.
